answer: Every identity docks at the registration wharf under an aged-domain flag: a DNSSEC-signed thread of TXT records on its own domain, creation date checked in public logs; post-cutoff domains rejected. Honest users pay twelve dollars a year, once. A Sybil farmer needs N domains with years of history, unbackdatable and unbulkmakeable: aged domains cost real money, fresh ones fail the age check, and one shared domain collapses its puppets to one flag. Each fake costs a market-priced domain, so attack expense grows linearly with N; the registry stays a haven while the wharf turns away the fleet.
